perRule.rule: No language word by spelling in the drawing path. In `ts/metalang/app.tsx` and `ts/metalang/client.tsx`, a word of a drawn language may not be written as a literal where it is used to look something up in the document being drawn or in its rulebook, and may not be written as a local constant renaming a word `ts/metalang/words.ts` already names. The only legal route to a language word in those two uses is a named constant in `words.ts` or a rulebook lookup. This stops a member's identity being taken from the spelling of a column — `member['name']`, `columns.includes('name')`, `=== 'name'` — instead of asking the rulebook. Where it stops. Tim set this boundary as written on 2026-11-11, answering `rule-1-boundary` with `lookups-and-renames` in pkg-a37618205163. Enforced on every word `words.ts` names, the rule flags twenty-four literals in `app.tsx`; fifteen are the defect and nine are these three kinds. RETRY NOTE. Nothing in the tree changed between the first attempt and this return; the first return was rejected on shape only (each `perRule.rule` now carries the approved rule text verbatim, with the fix-applied annotation moved into `diagnosticId`). Every proof above was re-run in the live tree for this return, and every figure quoted is from those runs.

WHAT CHANGED. One file, `/Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/.claude/worktrees/kit-walkthrough-targets/ts/metalang/guardrails.test.ts` (+629/-100). Nothing else in the tree is touched (`git status --short` shows that one file M). Nothing committed. No suppression, NoWarn, severity change or edit to violating production code.

FIX 1, rule 1's exemption was wider than the boundary. `ownWordsOf` (exempted a member of EVERY union of text literals a file declared, in any position) is replaced by `findingKindsOf` (:190). A union is the page's finding kinds only where the file says so by typing with it the property that says which list a thing came from — written out there, or through a type alias of the file's own. In app.tsx that finds exactly the two the finding names, `Said.from` and `Finding.from`; in client.tsx it finds none. Judgment call for the panel to rule on: the page's own word for that property is `from`, so the rule keys on a property signature named `from`. The findings forbid identifying the unions by a list of type names, and that is obeyed — no type name appears in the rule — but a future `from` on something that is not a finding would widen the exemption, which is the one way this mechanism can be wrong. The direction of error elsewhere is safe: where the rule cannot establish a union, it grants nothing and reports.

FIX 2, rule 2 read three routes and asserted that set complete. The claim is deleted; `writesIn` is rebuilt from what giving an attribute a value looks like, under both names the DOM gives an attribute. Routes read: markup; a property of an object a node is drawn from (which covers the props object handed to `createElement` and a props object spread into markup, because every non-test file is read, so the object is read at the site where it is written); a name handed to a call, with the DOM's own attribute-carrying calls read as the DOM declares them (`setAttribute` names at 0, `setAttributeNS` at 1, `toggleAttribute` carries an empty value); the property an assignment writes, onto a dataset or straight onto an object of attributes; `Object.assign` onto a dataset; and a run of text, for markup and for script carried to the browser as text (this tree's dataset use at propose.ts:786 and :789 is inside text). The bracket skip stays and the file says so where it does it.

WHAT THE RULE REPORTS AS UNREADABLE, and the boundary it stops at. Two directions: a name it knows, where it cannot read what that name is written onto; and a name it cannot read, where it knows the writing is onto a node's attributes (a dataset, a call that carries one, an object drawn into a node). It reports neither for a name it cannot read written onto something it does not know — that is every record keyed by a word in this tree, and says nothing about an identity attribute. That boundary is load-bearing: reporting every computed object key instead would raise three findings at words.ts:459 and check.ts:162-167 that no IMPLEMENT could clear, which would hold `bun test` red for good. The boundary is stated in the rule file at `drawnIntoANode` (:559).

TWO SMALLER CALLS, flagged rather than buried. (a) `Gives` lost its third state: an attribute written with no value beside it carries an empty value, which is written out as much as any other constant, so `<tr data-member />` and `toggleAttribute('data-member')` now both read as constant instead of one each way. (b) `writesIn` returns its findings in line order, because the code is read before the text and a reader of a finding reads down the file. Both are internal to the reading the two rules share; neither widens or narrows what the contract bans.

PRODUCTION RED — rule 1's impact, and nothing else. `bun test` is red on one test, `the drawing path > writes no word of the language out`, with the same fifteen literals as before this round. No diagnostic id exists (the contract approves no analyzer); the responsible rule is rule 1, reported by `wordsBySpelling`. Locations, all `ts/metalang/app.tsx`, each reported as "the language word \"<word>\" is written out; reach it through the constant words.ts names it by, or ask the rulebook": 363 "optional", 370 "id", 371 "is", 376 "properties", 379 "options", 385 "is", 386 "id", 543 "object", 1411 "properties", 1491 "is", 1493 "is", 1508 "options", 1510 "options", 1517 "properties", 1545 "language". The contract records these under `Rules to add` rule 1: "The fifteen are the rule's impact on existing code and IMPLEMENT clears them." Rules 2 and 3 are green against the whole tree: both tree-wide tests pass over all 22 non-test `ts/` files, so neither fix added a production finding. The .NET side is unaffected: `make build` exit 0 with 0 warnings and 0 errors, `make test` exit 0 (619 + 56 + 11 + 148 passed, 0 failed), `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint` both exit 0.

MEASUREMENT NOTE. A single-file `bun test` run always exits 1 in this repo: bunfig.toml turns coverage on with a 0.75 floor and one file cannot reach it. Proven on an untouched, fully green file — `bun test ts/metalang/words.test.ts` reports 77 pass / 0 fail and exits 1.
